description: K₅Na₃TaNb₇O₂₄ is (Cubic) Perovskite-derived structured and crystallizes in the monoclinic Cm space group. There are four inequivalent K sites. In the first K site, K is bonded to twelve O atoms to form KO₁₂ cuboctahedra that share corners with four equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, corners with eight equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with two equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with four equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra,  a faceface with one TaO₆ octahedra, and faces with seven NbO₆ octahedra. There are four shorter (2.85 Å) and eight longer (2.87 Å) K-O bond lengths. In the second K site, K is bonded to twelve O atoms to form KO₁₂ cuboctahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, corners with eight KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with two equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with four KO₁₂ cuboctahedra,  a faceface with one TaO₆ octahedra, and faces with seven NbO₆ octahedra. There are eight shorter (2.86 Å) and four longer (2.87 Å) K-O bond lengths. In the third K site, K is bonded to twelve O atoms to form KO₁₂ cuboctahedra that share corners with four equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, corners with eight equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with six KO₁₂ cuboctahedra,  a faceface with one TaO₆ octahedra, and faces with seven NbO₆ octahedra. There are four shorter (2.86 Å) and eight longer (2.87 Å) K-O bond lengths. In the fourth K site, K is bonded to twelve O atoms to form KO₁₂ cuboctahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, corners with eight equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with two equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with four equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra,  a faceface with one TaO₆ octahedra, and faces with seven NbO₆ octahedra. There are eight shorter (2.85 Å) and four longer (2.87 Å) K-O bond lengths. There are two inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded to twelve O atoms to form NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra that share corners with twelve KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with two equivalent KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with four equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra,  a faceface with one TaO₆ octahedra, and faces with seven NbO₆ octahedra. There are eight shorter (2.84 Å) and four longer (2.85 Å) Na-O bond lengths. In the second Na site, Na is bonded to twelve O atoms to form NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra that share corners with four equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, corners with eight KO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with two equivalent NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, faces with four KO₁₂ cuboctahedra,  a faceface with one TaO₆ octahedra, and faces with seven NbO₆ octahedra. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.84-2.86 Å. Ta is bonded to six O atoms to form TaO₆ octahedra that share corners with six NbO₆ octahedra, faces with three NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, and faces with five KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are a spread of Ta-O bond distances ranging from 2.00-2.02 Å. There are five inequivalent Nb sites. In the first Nb site, Nb is bonded to six O atoms to form NbO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent TaO₆ octahedra, corners with four equivalent NbO₆ octahedra, faces with three NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, and faces with five KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are five shorter (2.02 Å) and one longer (2.04 Å) Nb-O bond length. In the second Nb site, Nb is bonded to six O atoms to form NbO₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent TaO₆ octahedra, corners with four NbO₆ octahedra, faces with three NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, and faces with five KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are a spread of Nb-O bond distances ranging from 2.01-2.03 Å. In the third Nb site, Nb is bonded to six O atoms to form NbO₆ octahedra that share corners with six NbO₆ octahedra, faces with three NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, and faces with five KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are a spread of Nb-O bond distances ranging from 2.01-2.03 Å. In the fourth Nb site, Nb is bonded to six O atoms to form NbO₆ octahedra that share corners with six NbO₆ octahedra, faces with three NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, and faces with five KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are a spread of Nb-O bond distances ranging from 2.01-2.03 Å. In the fifth Nb site, Nb is bonded to six O atoms to form NbO₆ octahedra that share corners with six NbO₆ octahedra, faces with three NaO₁₂ cuboctahedra, and faces with five KO₁₂ cuboctahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. There are a spread of Nb-O bond distances ranging from 2.01-2.03 Å. There are fourteen inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to two K, two Na, one Ta, and one Nb atom. In the second O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to two K, two Na, and two Nb atoms. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to two K, two Na, and two Nb atoms. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to two K, two Na, and two Nb atoms. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to three K, one Na, one Ta, and one Nb atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to three K, one Na, and two Nb atoms. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to three K, one Na, and two Nb atoms. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to three K, one Na, and two Nb atoms. In the ninth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to four K, one Ta, and one Nb atom. In the tenth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to one K, three Na, one Ta, and one Nb atom. In the eleventh O site, O is bonded to four K and two Nb atoms to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing OK₄Nb₂ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedra are not tilted. In the twelfth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to one K, three Na, and two Nb atoms. In the thirteenth O site, O is bonded to four K and two Nb atoms to form distorted edge-sharing OK₄Nb₂ octahedra. In the fourteenth O site, O is bonded in a distorted linear geometry to one K, three Na, and two Nb atoms.
